```{r}
# -----------------------------
# 1) Helpers: SMD
# -----------------------------
smd_cont <- function(x, g){ # g: 0/1
  x0 <- x[g == 0]; x1 <- x[g == 1]
  m0 <- mean(x0, na.rm = TRUE); m1 <- mean(x1, na.rm = TRUE)
  s0 <- sd(x0, na.rm = TRUE);   s1 <- sd(x1, na.rm = TRUE)
  sp <- sqrt((s0^2 + s1^2) / 2)
  if (is.na(sp) || sp == 0) return(NA_real_)
  (m1 - m0) / sp
}

smd_bin <- function(ind, g){ # ind: 0/1 indicator for a given level
  p0 <- mean(ind[g == 0], na.rm = TRUE)
  p1 <- mean(ind[g == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
  p  <- mean(ind, na.rm = TRUE)
  den <- sqrt(p * (1 - p))
  if (is.na(den) || den == 0) return(NA_real_)
  (p1 - p0) / den
}

make_smd_map <- function(data, vars, gvar = "FU"){
  g <- data[[gvar]]
  out <- list()

  for (v in vars){
    x <- data[[v]]

    # continuous / numeric
    if (is.numeric(x)){
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- tibble(
        variable = v,
        row_type = "label",
        label = NA_character_,
        smd = smd_cont(x, g)
      )
      next
    }

    # categorical: per-level indicator SMD
    xf <- as.factor(x)
    levs <- levels(xf)
    for (L in levs){
      ind <- as.integer(xf == L)
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- tibble(
        variable = v,
        row_type = "level",
        label = L,
        smd = smd_bin(ind, g)
      )
    }
  }

  bind_rows(out) %>%
    mutate(smd_fmt = if_else(is.na(smd), "", sprintf("%.2f", smd)))
}

# -----------------------------
# 2) Baseline dataset + group
# -----------------------------
df0 <- Descriptives %>%
  mutate(
    FU = if_else(!is.na(ECSApp), 1L, 0L),  # 1 = responded at follow-up
    Group = factor(
      if_else(FU == 1L, "Follow-up respondents", "Baseline-only (attriters)"),
      levels = c("Follow-up respondents", "Baseline-only (attriters)")
    ),
    ActivityCriteriaYes = if_else(ActivityCriteriaYes == "Yes", 1, 0),
    SocialCriteriaYes   = if_else(SocialCriteriaYes   == "Yes", 1, 0)
  )

# (optional) force some 0/1 vars to be categorical if they are stored as numeric
force_categorical <- c("ActivityCriteriaYes", "SocialCriteriaYes")
df0 <- df0 %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(force_categorical), ~ factor(.x, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))))

# -----------------------------
# 3) 3-column table: Overall + respondents + attriters
# -----------------------------
tab3 <- df0 %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = Group,
    include = all_of(vars_baseline),
    type = list(
      Taux.de.couv.global ~ "continuous2",
      OpportunityCosts ~ "continuous2",
      PrescriptiveNorm ~ "continuous2",
      NumberChildren ~ "continuous2",
      MonthlyDaycareFees ~ "continuous2"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{p}% ({n})"
    ),
    digits = all_continuous() ~ 1,
    missing = "no",
    label = labels
  ) %>%
  add_overall(last = FALSE) %>%
  modify_header(
    label ~ "**Variable**",
    stat_0 ~ "**Overall (baseline)**",
    stat_1 ~ "**Follow-up respondents**",
    stat_2 ~ "**Baseline-only (attriters)**"
  )

# -----------------------------
# 4) Add SMD column (respondents vs attriters)
# -----------------------------
smd_map <- make_smd_map(
  data = df0 %>% mutate(FU = if_else(Group == "Follow-up respondents", 1L, 0L)),
  vars = vars_baseline,
  gvar = "FU"
)

tab3_smd <- tab3 %>%
  modify_table_body(~ .x %>%
    left_join(smd_map, by = c("variable", "row_type", "label")) %>%
    mutate(SMD = coalesce(smd_fmt, "")) %>%
    select(-smd, -smd_fmt)
  ) %>%
  modify_header(SMD ~ "**SMD**") %>%
  modify_footnote(
    SMD ~ "Standardized mean difference compares follow-up respondents vs baseline-only (attriters); for categorical variables, SMD is computed per level (indicator)."
  )

# -----------------------------
# 5) Export flextable
# -----------------------------
tab3_smd %>%
  as_flex_table() %>%
  italic(j = 1, part = "body") %>%
  set_caption("Attrition table: baseline overall vs respondents vs attriters, with SMD (respondents vs attriters)")

```

## Alluvial plot of the flow from Intention to access

```{r alluvialPlot}

# Ensure your data is in the correct format for ggalluvial
alluvial_data <- MainDB %>% 
 # Control %>% 
  dplyr::select(Intention, ECSApp, ECSUseYes) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Intention) & !is.na(ECSApp) & !is.na(ECSUseYes)) %>% 
  mutate(Intention = ifelse(Intention == "Yes", "Yes" , "No"),
           Application = ifelse(ECSApp == 1, "Applied", "Did not apply"), 
         Access = ifelse(ECSUseYes == 1, "Accessed", "Did not access")) 

# Create the alluvial plot
ggplot(alluvial_data,
       aes(axis1 = Intention, axis2 = Application, axis3 = Access)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = Intention), width = 1/12) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/12, fill = "gray") +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 3) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Intention (During Pregnancy)", "Application (One year later)", "Access (One year later)"),
                   expand = c(0.15, 0.15)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Flow of Early Childcare Intention to Actual Access",
       x = "Stages",
       y = "Number of Families") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Yes" =  "#D55E00", "No" = "#0072B2"))

```

# Results

## SES gaps in outcomes: Table for Supplementary Information

```{r}
library(fixest)
library(tidyr)

df <- MainDB %>%
  mutate(
    Intention = ifelse(Intention == "Yes", 1, 0),
    Educ = relevel(factor(Educ), ref = "Sup")
  )

m_gap <- feols(c(Intention, ECSApp, ECSUseYes) ~ Educ, data = df, se = "hetero")

tidy_fixest <- function(m, level = 0.95){
  ct <- as.data.frame(coeftable(m))
  ct$term <- rownames(ct); rownames(ct) <- NULL

  crit <- qnorm(1 - (1 - level)/2)

  ct %>%
    transmute(
      term,
      estimate = Estimate,
      std.error = `Std. Error`,
      conf.low  = estimate - crit * std.error,
      conf.high = estimate + crit * std.error
    )
}

mlist <- as.list(m_gap)
names(mlist) <- names(m_gap)

td <- bind_rows(lapply(names(mlist), function(nm){
  tidy_fixest(mlist[[nm]]) %>% mutate(outcome = nm)
}))

educ_terms <- td %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  distinct(term) %>%
  pull(term)

if(length(educ_terms) != 1){
  stop("Multiple Educ terms found. Set `educ_term` manually, e.g. educ_term <- 'EducBac'.")
}
educ_term <- educ_terms[1]

tab_si <- td %>%
  filter(term %in% c("(Intercept)", educ_term)) %>%
  mutate(term_clean = if_else(term == "(Intercept)", "Intercept", "GapTerm")) %>%
  select(outcome, term_clean, estimate, conf.low, conf.high) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = term_clean,
    values_from = c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Outcome = case_when(
      grepl("Intention", outcome) ~ "Intend to use",
      grepl("ECSApp", outcome) ~ "Apply",
      grepl("ECSUseYes", outcome) ~ "Access",
      TRUE ~ outcome
    ),
    Intercept = round(estimate_Intercept, 3),
    Intercept_CI = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf.low_Intercept, conf.high_Intercept),
    Gap = round(estimate_GapTerm, 3),
    Gap_CI = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf.low_GapTerm, conf.high_GapTerm),
    PercentDiff = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * abs(estimate_GapTerm) / estimate_Intercept)
  )
library(officer)


# tab_si is your tibble shown above
ft_si <- tab_si %>%
  mutate(
    Intercept = sprintf("%.3f", Intercept),
    Gap       = sprintf("%.3f", Gap)
  ) %>%
  flextable() %>%
  set_header_labels(
    Outcome = "Stage",
    Intercept = "High-SES rate",
    Intercept_CI = "95% CI",
    Gap = "Low–High (pp)",
    Gap_CI = "95% CI",
    PercentDiff = "Low vs High (%)"
  ) %>%
  align(j = c("Intercept","Intercept_CI","Gap","Gap_CI","PercentDiff"), align = "center", part = "all") %>%
  align(j = "Outcome", align = "left", part = "all") %>%
  autofit() %>%
  bold(part = "header") %>%
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") %>%
  theme_vanilla() %>%
  border_remove() %>%
  border_outer(border = fp_border(color = "black", width = 1)) %>%
  border_inner_h(border = fp_border(color = "black", width = 0.5)) %>%
  border_inner_v(border = fp_border(color = "black", width = 0.5)) %>%
  set_table_properties(layout = "autofit")

ft_si


```

## Results: Alternative models

### Oaxaca-Blinder with all predictors

#### Intention

##### Results and model performance

```{r }


# Create the database
db_intention_numeric_clean <- MLDummified %>%
  filter(!is.na(Intention)) %>%
  mutate(target = as.numeric(Intention) -1) %>% 
 select(-c(Assignment,  ECSApp, ECSUseYes, 
           Intention, EntryAgeBeforeOne, 
           BabyHealthIndex, MotherHealthIndex, #PoliticalOrientation,
           MovedOut,  
           ActivityCriteriaYes,
  SocialCriteriaYes,
  RegistrationOnlineOnly
 ))

# Preparation
## Split the sample

tidymodels_prefer()
set.seed(10)
split <- initial_split(db_intention_numeric_clean, prop = 0.8)
train <- training(split)
test <- testing(split)

# Clean the names
coef_names <- c(  
  "NumberChildren" = "Number of children in the household",
  "Taux.de.couv.global" = "Early childcare coverage in the area of residence",
  "ActiveYes" = "Mother is active before birth",
  "WorkPlanToYes" = "Mother wanted to work after birth",
  "ECAccessHoursFitYes" = "Early childcare opening hours fit",
  "AccessInformalFullTimeYes" = "Houshold has access to informal full-time childcare",
  "OpportunityCosts" = "Opportunity costs of staying at home for the mother",
  "NegativeImpactSalaryYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on salary",
  "NegativeImpactCareerYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on career",
  "NegativeImpactWellBeingYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on well-being",
  "PrescriptiveNorm" = "Number of people opposed to mother using childcare",
  "NormsUseMostToAllYes" = "The majority of friends and relatives use early childcare",
  "AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamilyYes" = "Traditional attitudes towards household roles",
  "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildrenYes" = "Believes work negatively affects children",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityOverestimate" = "Overestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityUnderestimate" = "Underestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "TrustEarlyChildcareAgreeYes" = "Household trusts early childcare",
  "ECBenefitChildrenAgreeYes" = "Household believes in early childcare benefits",
  "LevelInformationLow knowledge" = "Household has low knowledge about early childcare",
  "LevelComprehensionGoodExcellentYes" = "Mother's comprehension level of French is good/excellent",
  "PresentOrientedYes" = "The mother is present biased",
  "KnowsECIsSubsidizedYes" = "Household knows that early childcare is subsidized",
  "BelieveAccessingChildcareEasyYes" = "Household believes accessing childcare is easy",
  "HasAccessToAComputerYes" = "Household has access to a computer",
  "CanAccessScoialResourcesYes" = "Household can access social resources",
    "CanAccessInformationYes" = "Household can access information"
 # "EntryAgeBeforeOneBeforeOne" = "Household want to use early childcare after the child is 1 yo" # Dropped becuse colinear
)

# Define the recipe
model_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
  step_impute_knn(Taux.de.couv.global, NumberChildren, PrescriptiveNorm, neighbors = 5) %>% 
  step_YeoJohnson(NumberChildren, OpportunityCosts, PrescriptiveNorm)

# Call the regression function 
results_intention <- regression_all_table(train, test, model_recipe, coef_names, model_name = "Intention")

# Print the results
results_intention$model_summary  # Afficher le tableau récapitulatif

```

The performance of this model is:

```{r }
print(results_intention$performance)    # performance

```

We can plot these coefficients with a forest plot:

```{r, fig.cap= "Determinants of Early Childcare Intention. Forest plot of the coefficients of the OLS model with all predictors"}

# Create the forest plot
forest_plot <- create_forest_plot(
  results_intention$model_fit, 
  coef_names,
  title = "Determinants of Early Childcare Intention",
  subtitle = "Regression with all predictors"
)
print(forest_plot)

# save it if needed
#ggsave("forest_plot.png", forest_plot, width = 10, height = 8)
```

## Assignment forced models {#assignment-forced-models}

## Application

#####  {.unnumbered}

To confirm that the exclusion of treatment assignment by RFE reflects a stable modeling choice rather than an artifact of the variable-selection procedure, we compare the pooled regression coefficients (β) from the RFE-selected specification against the same specification with treatment assignment added.

For application, adding treatment assignment leaves every other coefficient in the model materially unchanged: the largest shift across all \[18\] predictors is 0.001, and the ranking of contributors by magnitude is identical. The coefficients on the two treatment-assignment dummies themselves are small relative to the other predictors in the model (β = -0.007 for the information-only arm; β = 0.030 for the information + support arm), consistent with RFE's decision not to retain either as a selected predictor. Notably, the difference in means between SES groups on treatment assignment (Mean(A) − Mean(B) = 0.012 and 0.001, respectively) is close to zero for both arms, as expected under successful randomization, which is itself a useful internal check on trial balance.

**Table S\_. Pooled coefficients with and without treatment assignment, Application**

| Variable | Code | β (RFE-selected) | β (+ Assignment) |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| Intention to use early childcare after birth | IntentionYes | 0.338 | 0.339 |
| Pre-birth employment status | ActiveYes | 0.208 | 0.207 |

## Access

##### Assignment forced models {.unnumbered}

To confirm that the exclusion of treatment assignment by RFE reflects a stable modeling choice rather than an artifact of the variable-selection procedure, we compare the pooled regression coefficients (β) from the RFE-selected specification against the same specification with treatment assignment added, for both application and access.

In both models, adding treatment assignment leaves every other coefficient materially unchanged: the largest shift across all predictors is 0.001 in either model, and the ranking of contributors by magnitude is unaffected. The coefficients on the two treatment-assignment dummies themselves are small relative to the other predictors in both models (application: β = -0.007 for the information-only arm, β = 0.030 for the information + support arm; access: β = 0.008 for both arms), consistent with RFE's decision not to retain either as a selected predictor in either outcome.

**Table S\_. Pooled coefficients with and without treatment assignment, Application**

| Pre-birth employment status | ActiveYes | 0.089 | 0.089 |
| Household income (low) | IncomeLess than 1500 euros | -0.090 | -0.090 |
| Household income (high) | IncomeMore than 2500 euros | 0.034 | 0.034 |
| Monthly childcare fees | MonthlyDaycareFees | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| Timing of application (before birth) | ECSAppTimingBeforeBirthYes | 0.095 | 0.095 |
| Intention to use early childcare after birth | IntentionYes | 0.085 | 0.084 |
| Parents called childcare centers | ApplicationCalledYes | 0.048 | 0.048 |
| Post-birth work intention | WorkPlanToYes | 0.037 | 0.038 |
| Exposure to childcare use in social network | NormsUseMostToAllYes | 0.040 | 0.040 |
| Household size (number of children) | NumberChildren | -0.029 | -0.029 |
| Social opposition to maternal childcare use | PrescriptiveNorm | -0.003 | -0.003 |
| Local early childcare availability | Taux.de.couv.global | 0.001 | 0.001 |
| Parents visited childcare centers | ApplicationWentOnSiteYesYes | 0.035 | 0.035 |
| Level of information about early childcare | LevelInformationLow knowledge | -0.063 | -0.063 |
| Parents networked | ApplicationNetworkedYes | 0.026 | 0.026 |
| Beliefs about work and child development | AttitudesLaborAffectsChildrenYes | -0.016 | -0.015 |
| Access to informal childcare arrangements | AccessInformalFullTimeYes | -0.047 | -0.047 |
| Knowledge of childcare subsidies | KnowsECIsSubsidizedYes | 0.057 | 0.056 |
| Gender role attitudes within the household | AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamilyYes | 0.025 | 0.025 |
| Trust in early childcare institutions | TrustEarlyChildcareAgreeYes | 0.007 | 0.008 |
| Perceived affordability (overestimation) | PerceivedAffordabilityOverestimate | 0.041 | 0.041 |
| Perceived affordability (underestimation) | PerceivedAffordabilityUnderestimate | -0.031 | -0.032 |
| Digital access | HasAccessToAComputerYes | -0.028 | -0.028 |
| Employment-based prioritization criteria | ActivityCriteriaYesYes | 0.079 | 0.078 |

*Note: β (RFE-selected) reproduces the pooled coefficients from Section 2.3; β (+ Assignment) adds treatment assignment (reference: control arm) to the same specification. Coefficient shifts across all non-Assignment predictors are ≤0.001 in absolute value in both models. MonthlyDaycareFees displays as 0.000 due to the scale of the underlying variable (mean difference measured in euros); reported with additional decimal places \[insert exact value\].*

Taken together, these results confirm that treatment assignment's exclusion from the main decomposition models is not an artifact of the RFE procedure: forcing it into either specification leaves all other estimated socioeconomic determinants of application and access essentially unchanged.

#### Classical regression

##### Application

```{r }

db_clean_application <- MLDummified_Controls %>%   
  filter(!is.na(ECSApp)) %>%
  mutate(target = as.numeric(ECSApp)) %>% 
  select(-c(ECSApp, ECSUseYes ))  # Take a look at the data with skimr 

  
# Preparation 
## Split the sample 

tidymodels_prefer()
set.seed(10) 
split <- initial_split(db_clean_application, prop = 0.8) 
train <- training(split) 
test <- testing(split)  # Apply the recipe (simplified) 

model_recipe_application <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train) %>%   
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
 step_impute_knn(Taux.de.couv.global,
                NumberChildren,
                PrescriptiveNorm,
                neighbors = 5) %>% 
  step_YeoJohnson(MotherHealthIndex,
                  BabyHealthIndex,
                  NumberChildren, 
                  OpportunityCosts,
                  PrescriptiveNorm
                  )

# Clean the names
coef_names_application <- c(
  "IntentionYes" = "Intention: Household wants to use early childcare after birth",
  "NumberChildren" = "Number of children in the household",
  "Taux.de.couv.global" = "Early childcare coverage in the area of residence",
  "ActiveYes" = "Mother is active before birth",
  "WorkPlanToYes" = "Mother wanted to work after birth",
  "ECAccessHoursFitYes" = "Early childcare opening hours fit",
  "AccessInformalFullTimeYes" = "Houshold has access to informal full-time childcare",
  "OpportunityCosts" = "Opportunity costs of staying at home for the mother",
  "NegativeImpactSalaryYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on salary",
  "NegativeImpactCareerYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on career",
  "NegativeImpactWellBeingYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on well-being",
  "PrescriptiveNorm" = "Number of people opposed to mother using childcare",
  "NormsUseMostToAllYes" = "The majority of friends and relatives use early childcare",
  "AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamilyYes" = "Traditional attitudes towards household roles",
  "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildrenYes" = "Believes work negatively affects children",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityOverestimate" = "Overestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityUnderestimate" = "Underestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "TrustEarlyChildcareAgreeYes" = "Household trusts early childcare",
  "ECBenefitChildrenAgreeYes" = "Household believes in early childcare benefits",
  "LevelInformationLow knowledge" = "Household has low knowledge about early childcare",
  "LevelComprehensionGoodExcellentYes" = "Mother's comprehension level of French is good/excellent",
  "PresentOrientedYes" = "The mother is present biased",
  "KnowsECIsSubsidizedYes" = "Household knows that early childcare is subsidized",
  "BelieveAccessingChildcareEasyYes" = "Household believes accessing childcare is easy",
  "HasAccessToAComputerYes" = "Household has access to a computer",
  "CanAccessScoialResourcesYes" = "Household can access social resources",
  "CanAccessInformationYes" = "Household can access information",
  "MotherHealthIndex" = "Mother's health index at endline",
  "BabyHealthIndex" = "Baby's health index at endline",
  "EntryAgeBeforeOneBefore One" = "Want to use early childcare before the child is 1 yo",
 "MovedOutYes" = "Household moved between baseline and endline", 
   "ActivityCriteriaYesYes" = "Active mothers are prioritized",
  "SocialCriteriaYesYes" = "Vulnerable families are prioritized",
  "RegistrationOnlineOnlyYes" = "Registration is online only" 

)

# Call the regression function 
results_application <- regression_all_table(train, 
                                            test, 
                                            model_recipe_application,                                                  coef_names_application, 
                                            model_name = "Application")

# Print the results
results_application$model_summary
```

# Childcare types by SES

```{r}

# 1. Build childcare-type variable, conditional on access, restricted to control arm
QualityDB <- MainDB %>%
  mutate(
    ChildcareTypeDetailed = case_when(
      UseCrecheMuni >= 1 ~ "Municipal daycare",
      UseCrecheA    >= 1 ~ "Associative daycare",
      UsePrivée     >= 1 ~ "Private daycare",
      UseAssMat     >= 1 ~ "Childminder",
      UseCreche > 0 & UseCrecheMuni + UseCrecheA + UsePrivée == 0 ~ "Other daycare",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    SES_group = case_when(
  Educ2 == "Bac" ~ "Low-SES",
  Educ2 == "Sup" ~ "High-SES",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
),
    ChildcareTypeDetailed = factor(ChildcareTypeDetailed,
                                   levels = c("Municipal daycare","Associative daycare",
                                              "Private daycare","Other daycare","Childminder")),
    SES_group = factor(SES_group, levels = c("Low-SES","High-SES"))  # match your main coding
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ChildcareTypeDetailed))

# 2. Check cell sizes before testing
table(QualityDB$SES_group, QualityDB$ChildcareTypeDetailed)

n_low  <- sum(QualityDB$SES_group == "Low-SES")
n_high <- sum(QualityDB$SES_group == "High-SES")

# 3. Per-category counts, percentages, and pairwise tests (Low vs High)
type_levels <- levels(QualityDB$ChildcareTypeDetailed)

results <- map_dfr(type_levels, function(t) {
  
  count_low  <- sum(QualityDB$SES_group == "Low-SES"  & QualityDB$ChildcareTypeDetailed == t)
  count_high <- sum(QualityDB$SES_group == "High-SES" & QualityDB$ChildcareTypeDetailed == t)
  
  pct_low  <- 100 * count_low  / n_low
  pct_high <- 100 * count_high / n_high
  diff     <- pct_high - pct_low
  
  # Use Fisher's exact for small cells, prop.test otherwise
  tab2x2 <- matrix(c(count_low, n_low - count_low,
                     count_high, n_high - count_high),
                   nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  
  expected_min <- suppressWarnings(min(chisq.test(tab2x2)$expected))
  test <- if (is.na(expected_min) || expected_min < 5) {
    fisher.test(tab2x2)
  } else {
    prop.test(c(count_low, count_high), c(n_low, n_high), correct = TRUE)
  }
  
  stars <- case_when(
    test$p.value < 0.01 ~ "***",
    test$p.value < 0.05 ~ "**",
    test$p.value < 0.10 ~ "*",
    TRUE ~ ""
  )
  
  tibble(
    `Childcare type` = t,
    `Low-SES (%)`  = round(pct_low, 1),
    `High-SES (%)` = round(pct_high, 1),
    `Difference (pp)` = paste0(sprintf("%+.1f", diff), stars),
    `p-value` = signif(test$p.value, 3)
  )
})

# 4. Build flextable for Word export
ft <- flextable(results) %>%
  align(j = "Low-SES (%)",     align = "right", part = "body") %>%
  align(j = "High-SES (%)",    align = "right", part = "body") %>%
  align(j = "Difference (pp)", align = "right", part = "body") %>%
  align(j = "p-value",         align = "right", part = "body") %>%
  align(part = "header", align = "left") %>%
  width(j = "Childcare type",     width = 3.5, unit = "cm") %>%
  width(j = "Low-SES (%)",        width = 2.2, unit = "cm") %>%
  width(j = "High-SES (%)",       width = 2.2, unit = "cm") %>%
  width(j = "Difference (pp)",    width = 2.2, unit = "cm") %>%
  width(j = "p-value",            width = 2.0, unit = "cm") %>%
  padding(j = "Difference (pp)", padding.left = 15, part = "body") %>%
  add_footer_lines(paste0(
    "Note: Percentages of households using each childcare type, conditional on access, ",
    "by SES group, control arm only (unweighted; N low-SES = ", n_low,
    ", N high-SES = ", n_high, "). Difference = High-SES % minus Low-SES %. ",
    "Significance from two-sided Fisher's exact test (or chi-squared test where expected ",
    "cell counts >= 5) for each type vs. all others: * p<0.10, ** p<0.05, *** p<0.01."
  )) %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit()

print(ft)
#doc <- read_docx() %>% body_add_flextable(ft)
#print(doc, target = "SI_ChildcareType_by_SES_controlarm.docx")
```

```{r}
# Add WorkMotherFullTime and WorkMotherReduced to the intensity Oaxaca
# These go ONLY in the Oaxaca step — no need to re-run RFE

model_variables_intensity_extended <- c(
  cleaned_variables_intensity,   # MonthlyDaycareFees, Income, TrustEarlyChildcareAgree, NumberChildren, Intention
  "WorkMotherFullTime",
  "WorkMotherReduced"
)

oaxaca_data_intensity_extended <- Oaxaca_Intensity %>%
  filter(!is.na(ECSIntensity), ECSIntensity > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    target   = as.numeric(ECSIntensity),
    Educ_bin = as.numeric(Educ == "Sup")
  ) %>%
  select(target, Educ_bin, all_of(model_variables_intensity_extended))

formula_intensity_extended <- as.formula(
  paste("target ~", 
        paste(model_variables_intensity_extended, collapse = " + "), 
        "| Educ_bin")
)

set.seed(120)
oax_decomp_intensity_extended <- oaxaca(
  formula = formula_intensity_extended,
  data    = oaxaca_data_intensity_extended,
  R       = 100
)


coef_names_intensity <- c(
  "IntentionYes" = "Intention to use early childcare after birth",

  "NumberChildren" = "Household size (number of children)",
  
  "MonthlyDaycareFees" = "Monthly childcare fees",

  
  "TrustEarlyChildcareAgreeYes" = "Trust in early childcare institutions",
  
  "IncomeLess than 1500 euros" = "Household income (low)",
  "IncomeMore than 2500 euros" = "Household income (high)",
  "WorkMotherFullTimeYes" = "The mother works full time",
  "WorkMotherReducedTRUE" = "The mother reduced her working hours after delivery"

)
# Compare income contributions with and without work variables
# Look specifically at whether Income coefficients change
plot_oaxaca_gap(oax_decomp_intensity_extended, outcome = "Intensity (with work vars)")
plot_top_contributors(oax_decomp_intensity_extended,
                      var_labels = coef_names_intensity,
                      top_n = 10,
                      outcome = "Intensity (with work vars)")
```
